title: Owl silent flight — serrated feathers
problem_statement: Aircraft and fan noise limits operations near people. The problem is documented and scoped before any solution work begins.
concept: Owls fly silently thanks to serrated leading-edge feathers that break turbulence into smaller vortices. Researchers apply serrations to fan blades and airfoils to cut noise. Constraint emphasis: the listed constraints are the design drivers — solve the hardest one first.
novelty_assessment: Noise reduction via leading-edge geometry rather than slower speeds.
validation_plan: Anechoic noise measurement vs smooth blades
Efficiency penalty quantification

title: Intermodal container — McLean (1956)
problem_statement: Break-bulk cargo handling was slow, theft-prone, and expensive. The problem is documented and scoped before any solution work begins.
concept: Malcolm McLean's 1956 standardized shipping container moved the handling problem from cargo to box: cranes, ships, trains, and trucks all speak container. Global trade's physical API. Constraint emphasis: the listed constraints are the design drivers — solve the hardest one first.
novelty_assessment: Standardization as the invention, not any single machine.
validation_plan: Port turnaround times before/after containerization (historical)
Document the outcome honestly whether it confirms or kills the concept.

title: TRIZ principle 1 — segmentation
problem_statement: A monolithic object is hard to handle, repair, or adapt. The problem is documented and scoped before any solution work begins.
concept: Divide an object into independent parts: sectional furniture, modular phones, microservices. Segmentation trades one big problem for many small manageable ones.

validation_plan: List 3 products improved by segmentation in your field

title: Shinkansen nose — kingfisher beak
problem_statement: Bullet trains exiting tunnels at speed produced a sonic-boom-like tunnel boom that broke noise regulations.
concept: Engineer and birdwatcher Eiji Nakatsu redesigned the Shinkansen nose after the kingfisher's beak — a shape that moves between air and water without a splash. The boom vanished, speed rose, and energy use fell. Crossover note: the power here is the domain transfer — state explicitly what each domain contributes.
novelty_assessment: Cross-domain transfer by a hobbyist's eye: fluid dynamics shared between beaks and trains.
validation_plan: Wind-tunnel pressure-wave measurement
Energy-per-trip comparison
